payer.name: Tessara Health Plan
payer.hours: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time, every day

fonts.family: 'Noto Sans', 'Inter', 'Noto Sans SC', 'Noto Sans KR', sans-serif

cover.notABillText: This notice explains how your plan handled the claims your providers sent us. Any balance you still owe is between you and the provider; we do not collect it.
cover.specimenLine: Synthetic test document — not issued by any health plan
cover.intro: Thank you for being a member of {planName}. This notice covers claims we processed between {periodStart} and {periodEnd}. Please look it over and keep it with your health records.
cover.totalsNote: Plan approved = Plan paid + Most you may be billed. You never owe more than the plan-approved amount to a plan provider.
cover.moopText: Your copayments and coinsurance for covered medical services count toward this limit. When you reach it, you pay nothing more for the plan's covered medical services during the rest of the calendar year.
cover.noDeductible: Your plan has no medical deductible.
cover.callTitle: Questions? We are here to help.

claims.title: Details about your claims
claims.intro: For each claim we show every service on it. Each code in the Notes column is explained beneath the claims on the same page.
claims.pageContinues: More claims on the next page

info.title: About this notice

terms.text: What the provider billed for the service. This is often more than the plan approves.
The amount the plan has agreed to pay plan providers for a covered service. A plan provider accepts it as full payment.
Your copayment or coinsurance for the service. It is the most the provider may bill you.

hmo: Get your care from plan providers. Except for emergency and urgently needed care, services from providers outside the plan are generally not covered.
Your primary care provider coordinates your care. Some services need a referral or the plan's approval first.
info.questionsTitle: If something does not look right
questions: Call the provider's office if a bill does not match the amount in the column Most you may be billed.
Call us at {phone} (TTY {tty}) if a claim looks wrong. We can review it with you.
You can appeal when we decide not to pay, or to pay less, for your care. Each such decision comes with its own written notice that lists the steps and the time limit.

Free counseling about your Medicare coverage is available from the State Health Insurance Assistance Programs (SHIPs). You can also call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227); TTY users can call 1-877-486-2048.
info.deniedTitle: About services we did not cover
denied: We did not cover some services on this notice, and their notes say why. A written denial notice will follow, telling you how to appeal and how long you have to do it.
fraud: Watch for services you never received, the same service listed twice, or a provider you never saw.
Report anything suspicious to our Special Investigations line at {fraudPhone} (TTY {tty}), or call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227); TTY users can call 1-877-486-2048.
Keep your member ID card safe, as you would a credit card.

notices.title: Important information about your rights
nondiscrimination: {legalName} complies with all applicable federal civil rights laws, including Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act (Section 1557). {legalName} does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including limited English proficiency and primary language), age, disability, or sex (consistent with the scope of sex discrimination described at 45 CFR § 92.101(a)(2)).
In compliance with Section 1557 and other federal civil rights laws, we provide individuals the following in a timely manner and free of charge:

nondiscriminationServices.text: {legalName} will provide language assistance services for individuals with limited English proficiency (including individuals' companions with limited English proficiency) to ensure meaningful access to our programs, activities, services, and other benefits. Language assistance services may include:

{legalName} will provide appropriate auxiliary aids and services for individuals with disabilities (including individuals' companions with disabilities) to ensure effective communication. Appropriate auxiliary aids and services may include:
items: Qualified interpreters, including American Sign Language interpreters
Information in alternate formats (including but not limited to large print, recorded audio, and accessible electronic formats)

nondiscriminationServices.text: {legalName} will provide reasonable modifications for qualified individuals with disabilities, when necessary to ensure accessibility and equal opportunity to participate in our programs, activities, services, or other benefits.

nondiscriminationAfter: To ask for any of this help, call {phone} (TTY {tty}), {hours}.
For additional assistance, you may also contact our Section 1557 Coordinator at 520-555-0163 (TTY 711).
grievance: If you believe {legalName} has failed to provide these services or has discriminated in another way on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability, you can:
1. File a grievance with {legalName}. To do so, write to, call or email our Section 1557 Coordinator (details at right), or visit in person; the Coordinator can help you prepare it.

2. File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights: Electronically: https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/smartscreen/main.jsf. Via mail: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, 200 Independence Avenue, S.W. – 509F, Washington, D.C. 20201.
